```{r}
library(fieldborders)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The object metric

Field boundaries are judged by whether each field comes out as one object. `fb_evaluate()`
uses the object metric of the Fields of The World (FTW) benchmark:

* reference fields are the 4-connected shapes of the field-interior class of the
  reference raster, and delineated fields the objects of `fb_delineate()`;
* a delineated and a reference field match when their intersection over union (IoU)
  exceeds 0.5. Above 0.5 a field can match at most one other, so the matching is one to
  one without any assignment step;
* object precision is the share of delineated fields that match, object recall the share
  of reference fields that are matched, and F1 their harmonic mean. Delineated fields that
  lie mostly (more than half) in unlabelled reference pixels are not counted as false
  positives, so that partial reference maps can be used.

`fb_evaluate()` returns counts, which add up over tiles; `fb_accuracy()` turns them into
rates, including the recall of reference fields by size class:

```{r}
s <- fb_example_stack("california")
f <- fb_example_files("california")
ref <- fb_reference(sf::st_read(f$fields, quiet = TRUE), s)
m <- fb_model_pretrained("general")
fields <- fb_delineate(fb_tbc_maps(s, m), thresholds = m$thresholds)
ev <- fb_evaluate(ref, fields)
ev[, c("tp", "fp", "fn", "obj_tp", "obj_fp", "obj_fn", "n_pred")]
fb_accuracy(ev)[, c("reference_fields", "predicted_fields", "obj_precision", "obj_recall", "obj_f1")]
```

Summing counts over tiles before computing the rates, as `fb_accuracy()` does, weights
every field equally, whatever the tile it lies in.

## Uncertainty and comparisons

Fields in one tile share imagery, crops and management, so tiles, not fields, are the
units to resample. `fb_bootstrap()` draws tiles with replacement (within strata, if
given) and uses the same draws for the two methods of a comparison. To show the
interface, the California example is cut into four quarters, standing in for tiles:

```{r}
quarters <- function(r) {
  e <- as.vector(terra::ext(r)); xm <- mean(e[1:2]); ym <- mean(e[3:4])
  list(terra::ext(e[1], xm, ym, e[4]), terra::ext(xm, e[2], ym, e[4]),
       terra::ext(e[1], xm, e[3], ym), terra::ext(xm, e[2], e[3], ym))
}
dl <- fb_read_probabilities(f$prue)
fu <- fb_model_pretrained("general", "fusion")
methods <- list(TBC = fields,
                `TBC + PRUE B3` = fb_delineate(fb_fuse(fb_tbc_maps(s, m), dl, fu), thresholds = fu$thresholds))
counts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(quarters(ref)), function(k) {
  e <- quarters(ref)[[k]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(methods), function(nm)
    cbind(tile = k, method = nm, fb_evaluate(terra::crop(ref, e), terra::crop(methods[[nm]], e)))))
}))
fb_accuracy(counts, by = "method")[, c("method", "obj_precision", "obj_recall", "obj_f1")]
fb_bootstrap(counts, c("TBC + PRUE B3", "TBC"), B = 1000)
```

With four tiles the interval is meaningless; the validation below used 44 to 54 test tiles
per region.

## The validation study

The method was developed in California and validated in three regions on tiles of
512 x 512 pixels (3.1 km north to south and 2.1 to 3.1 km east to west). In each region
the tiles were assigned to fitting, tuning and test sets in blocks of 0.2 degrees, so
that neighbouring tiles fell into the same set. Models were fitted on the fitting tiles,
the input months of the deep model and all thresholds were chosen on the tuning tiles,
and the test tiles were evaluated once:

* **California 2024**: reference fields from the California Department of Water
  Resources Statewide Crop Mapping 2024; 120 tiles in four farming regions (44 fitting,
  22 tuning and 54 test tiles, with 3,696 reference fields).
* **Washington**: reference fields from the Washington State Department of Agriculture
  agricultural land use map, with imagery of 2024 or 2025, the year in which most fields
  of a tile were surveyed; 90 tiles in the irrigated Columbia Basin, the dryland farming
  of the Palouse and the Yakima Valley (31 fitting, 15 tuning and 44 test tiles, with
  2,155 reference fields). Models were fitted and tuned on Washington tiles.
* **Brazil 2019/20**: reference fields from the crop maps of the Brazilian National
  Supply Company (CONAB) for summer crops in Tocantins and irrigated rice in Rio Grande do
  Sul; 60 tiles (13 tuning and 47 test tiles, with 594 reference fields). These maps
  outline only the mapped crop, so most fields in a tile are unlabelled and object
  precision says little; object recall is the measure that counts. The models were
  fitted and tuned on California and Washington tiles, without any Brazilian labels.

The deep models are the FTW PRUE models with EfficientNet-B3 (trained on CC-BY data) and
EfficientNet-B7 encoders, applied to two monthly scenes: March and July in California,
May and August in Washington (chosen on the tuning tiles) and September and January in
Brazil. "Object procedure" means that their probabilities were turned into fields with
the same seeds, watershed and size filter as TBC. The FTW global field map and, in
California, the USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries were evaluated on the same tiles without
any fitting.

```{r, fig.height = 4.6}
acc <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "validation", "object_accuracy.csv", package = "fieldborders"))
va <- acc[acc$analysis == "primary", ]
f1 <- va$primary_metric == "obj_f1"
va$value <- ifelse(f1, va$obj_f1, va$obj_recall)
va$lo <- ifelse(f1, va$f1_lo, va$recall_lo)
va$hi <- ifelse(f1, va$f1_hi, va$recall_hi)
va$panel <- factor(paste(va$region, ifelse(f1, "(object F1)", "(object recall)")),
                   levels = c("California (object F1)", "Washington (object F1)", "Brazil (object recall)"))
va$method <- factor(va$method, levels = c("USDA Crop Sequence Boundaries", "FTW global field map", "PRUE B3",
                                          "PRUE B3 + object procedure", "PRUE B7 + object procedure",
                                          "Multi-temporal Canny + object procedure", "TBC", "TBC + PRUE B3",
                                          "TBC + PRUE B7"))
cols <- c(`Existing product` = "#5F5F5F", `Deep model` = "#3A7DC9", `Edge-detection baseline` = "#9A7BB5",
          TBC = "#C8323F", `TBC + deep model` = "#8E1B26")
ggplot(va, aes(value, method, colour = family)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = sprintf("%.2f", value)), hjust = -0.3, size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, breaks = names(cols), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.85), breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.2)) +
  labs(x = "Object accuracy with 95 % bootstrap interval (IoU > 0.5)", y = NULL) +
  fb_theme(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
v <- function(region, method, metric = "obj_f1") sprintf("%.2f", va[va$region == region & va$method == method, metric])
```

The results differ between the regions:

* In **California**, TBC without any deep model reached an object F1 of
  `r v("California", "TBC")`, above the CC-BY PRUE model with or without the object
  procedure (`r v("California", "PRUE B3 + object procedure")` and
  `r v("California", "PRUE B3")`), the FTW global map (`r v("California", "FTW global field map")`)
  and the multi-temporal Canny edges given the same cropland map and object procedure
  (`r v("California", "Multi-temporal Canny + object procedure")`); it did not differ
  clearly from PRUE B7 with the object procedure (`r v("California", "PRUE B7 + object procedure")`).
  Fusing TBC with PRUE B3 or B7 gave the highest F1 (`r v("California", "TBC + PRUE B3")`
  and `r v("California", "TBC + PRUE B7")`).
* In **Washington**, TBC split many fields into fragments (object precision
  `r v("Washington", "TBC", "obj_precision")`), most of all in the dryland farming of the
  Palouse. Its F1 of `r v("Washington", "TBC")` was below that of PRUE B3 and B7 with the
  object procedure (`r v("Washington", "PRUE B3 + object procedure")` and
  `r v("Washington", "PRUE B7 + object procedure")`) and of the FTW global map
  (`r v("Washington", "FTW global field map")`), and level with the Canny edges. The F1 of
  the fusion (`r v("Washington", "TBC + PRUE B3")` with B3) was higher than that of TBC
  alone and of the FTW global map, but not higher than that of the deep models with the
  object procedure.
* In **Brazil**, with models from California and Washington, TBC and its fusion with B3
  recovered more reference fields (object recall `r v("Brazil", "TBC", "obj_recall")` and
  `r v("Brazil", "TBC + PRUE B3", "obj_recall")`) than PRUE B3 with the object procedure
  (`r v("Brazil", "PRUE B3 + object procedure", "obj_recall")`) and the FTW global map
  (`r v("Brazil", "FTW global field map", "obj_recall")`). The gain came from the irrigated
  rice of Rio Grande do Sul; for the summer crops of Tocantins, recall was similar or lower.
  All methods recovered fewer than a third of the reference fields.

In Washington, the tuning chose the largest minimum field size of the pre-specified grid
(50 pixels, about 0.14 ha) for TBC. In a secondary analysis, added after these results
were seen, the thresholds of TBC, PRUE with the object procedure and their fusion were
tuned again on the Washington tuning tiles over the wider grid used for the pretrained
models (minimum field sizes up to 400 pixels), and the test tiles were evaluated again:

```{r}
ex <- acc[acc$analysis != "primary", ]
ex$`F1 (95 % CI)` <- sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", ex$obj_f1, ex$f1_lo, ex$f1_hi)
ex$Precision <- round(ex$obj_precision, 2)
ex$Recall <- round(ex$obj_recall, 2)
knitr::kable(ex[, c("method", "Precision", "Recall", "F1 (95 % CI)")], row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Method (Washington, wider grid)", "Precision", "Recall", "F1 (95 % CI)"))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
w <- function(method) sprintf("%.2f", ex$obj_f1[ex$method == method])
```

With the wider grid, TBC split far fewer fields: its F1 rose to `r w("TBC")`, level with
PRUE B3 with the object procedure (`r w("PRUE B3 + object procedure")`), and the fusion with
B3 reached `r w("TBC + PRUE B3")`. PRUE B7 with the object procedure
(`r w("PRUE B7 + object procedure")`) remained more accurate than TBC, and its fusion with
TBC (`r w("TBC + PRUE B7")`) did not improve on it. Much of the gap in the pre-specified
comparison therefore came from the thresholds, chiefly the minimum field size: on the
tuning tiles, a larger minimum raised the F1 of TBC markedly but hardly changed that of
the deep model. Because this analysis was chosen after the results were known, it does
not replace the pre-specified comparison.

TBC is therefore a strong method where it was developed and a useful complement to the
deep models, but it is not uniformly better than they are, and its accuracy depends on
the minimum field size. Where reference fields of the target region exist, train a local
model (`vignette("training")`), tune its thresholds over a wide grid and compare TBC, the
deep model and their fusion on separate tiles before mapping a large area.

## The pretrained models

The pretrained models of the package were fitted with `fb_train()` and `fb_fit_fusion()`
on the fitting tiles of California and of California and Washington together, and their
thresholds were tuned with `fb_tune()` on the tuning tiles, over a wider grid than in the
validation above (minimum field sizes up to 400 pixels instead of 50). On the test tiles,
which were not used to fit or tune them:

```{r}
pm <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "validation", "pretrained_models.csv", package = "fieldborders"))
tab <- data.frame(Model = pm$model, `Test tiles` = sprintf("%s (%d)", pm$region, pm$tiles), Method = pm$method,
                  Fields = pm$reference_fields, Precision = round(pm$obj_precision, 2),
                  Recall = round(pm$obj_recall, 2),
                  `F1 [95 % CI]` = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", pm$obj_f1, pm$f1_lo, pm$f1_hi),
                  `Recall < 1 ha` = round(pm$recall_s1, 3), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tab)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
p <- function(model, region, method, col = "obj_f1") {
  sprintf("%.3f", pm[pm$model == model & pm$region == region & pm$method == method, col])
}
```

With a minimum field size of about 1.1 ha, the pretrained models find almost none of the
reference fields smaller than 1 ha, but they split few fields. In Washington, the
`"general"` model reached an F1 of `r p("general", "Washington", "TBC")` alone and
`r p("general", "Washington", "TBC + PRUE B3")` fused with PRUE B3, close to the models
fitted and tuned on Washington alone over the same grid (secondary analysis above). The R
implementation reproduces the pipeline used for the validation: with the same design, the
validation pipeline reached an F1 of `r p("california", "California", "TBC", "pipeline_obj_f1")`
with TBC and `r p("california", "California", "TBC + PRUE B3", "pipeline_obj_f1")` with the
fusion on the California test tiles, against `r p("california", "California", "TBC")` and
`r p("california", "California", "TBC + PRUE B3")` for the `"california"` models of the
package.
